title: The Sky Decides
clue: You will not know what today's walk is until you open the door and look up.
reveal: Write seven weather rules on an envelope. Today's sky picks the rule, and your dog sets the pace inside it. If the weather is too wild, the rule is a warm blanket and a sniff of the open window.
objective: Write a set of weather rules, open the door, read the sky, follow the matching rule with your dog leading, and write their best moment on the envelope in one word.
instructions:
Take an envelope and write these seven rules on the back, one line each.
• SUN: find the warm patch and let your dog sniff and rest there.
• WIND: stand still at a sheltered corner and let the nose read it.
• DRIZZLE: a short, slow sniff under an awning or hedge.
• FOG: a whisper walk on a street you know, close and slow; name the first landmark that appears out of the mist.
• FROST: slow steps off salted ground, paws checked.
• OVERCAST: your dog picks every corner.
• STAY IN: a warm blanket and a sniff of the open window.
Hang the envelope by the door. Tonight, or tomorrow, whenever you feel like it, you will open the door and see.

Open the door and read the sky aloud like a captain: 'Overcast, light wind.' The matching rule picks the walk. If two fit, turn toward each and follow your dog's nose. Then wait a quiet minute at the open door: if your dog settles on the mat instead, that is STAY IN, and a dog who rushes the door every time is simply a Go.
Walk the rule. Every rule has one long sniff stop with no goal and a rest before you head home. Your dog sets the pace, and if they want to turn round, you do.
Look for what the weather changes: wind brings new smells, fog muffles sound, frost crackles underfoot. Tell your dog the one you spot.

Back home, cross out the rule you used and write your dog's best moment beside it in one word. Read it aloud once by the door, then put the envelope back: the other rules wait until the sky picks them.
twist: Extreme weather is a rule too: if the sky says stay in, the rule is a warm blanket and a sniff of the open window, and that gets crossed out as well.
variations: Doorstep: do the whole rule on your balcony, step or by an open window, letting your dog sniff the air.
Season-long: leave the envelope on the hook all season and see how many rules the sky picks. No order and no deadline.
Senior dog: halve every rule to a few minutes and one stop.
Add your own rule for snow, first leaves or a rainbow, in your own handwriting.
completion: You have read the sky and walked or stayed in by its rule, and one word is on the envelope. Turning back after two minutes counts.
photoIdea: Your dog with the sky behind them, taken in a pause when they are already standing still. The weather is the subject.
memoryPrompt: What was the sky doing, and what was your dog's one word?
safety: Skip the walk in storms, lightning, heavy rain, ice, or heat where the sidewalk fails a hand test.
In frost, wipe paws after salt and de-icer; in fog or dusk, wear reflective gear and a steady light.
Keep clear of trees in wind, and skip puddles in case of oil or antifreeze.
